questions.title: IRCTC / Railway Ticketing System — DB Schema + SQL + Concurrent Booking
questions.answer:
Concurrency strategy: JPA @Version (optimistic locking) for low-contention routes. For peak-time (tatkal), use Redis distributed lock (Redisson) with 30s TTL: SETNX seat:lock:{seatId} userId EX 30. Lock acquired → book → release. Lock not acquired → seat taken.
Scaling: Read replicas for availability queries. Write to primary only. Partition Seat table by train_id. Cache popular route seat counts in Redis (invalidate on booking).

questions.title: Idempotent Booking + Double Payment Prevention
questions.answer:
Full flow:
1. Client generates UUID idempotencyKey per booking attempt.
2. API: POST /bookings with header Idempotency-Key: uuid.
3. Server atomically SET booking:idem:{key} PROCESSING NX EX 300 in Redis.
4. If key already exists → check if value is DONE:{bookingId} → return cached response (200).
5. Process booking → charge payment → store result as DONE:{bookingId} in Redis with 24h TTL.
6. Also store idempotency_key as UNIQUE column in Booking table — second layer of safety.

For the payment charge itself: Payment gateway also supports idempotency keys. Pass the same key so even if you call the payment gateway twice (network retry), only one charge occurs.

Outbox Pattern (for reliable event publishing): Write booking + outbox event in same DB transaction. Separate poller reads outbox and publishes to Kafka. Guarantees event is published exactly once even if service crashes.

questions.title: URL Shortener / TinyURL — Production Design
questions.answer:
Core design: Auto-increment ID → Base62 encode → 6-char short code (62^6 = 56 billion URLs).

DB Schema: url_mapping(id BIGINT PK AUTO_INCREMENT, short_code VARCHAR(8) UNIQUE, long_url TEXT, user_id BIGINT, expires_at DATETIME, created_at TIMESTAMP)

Redirect flow: GET /{code} → Redis GET url:{code} (cache hit ~2ms) → miss → DB query → cache set (TTL 7 days) → HTTP 301 redirect.

Auth for MMT variant: JWT in request → extract userId → verify url_mapping.user_id == requestUserId → else 403.

Scale: 100B URLs/day redirect reads → Redis cluster. Writes: ~10M/day → single MySQL primary is fine. Use CDN in front for global redirect acceleration. Analytics: async Kafka event on each redirect → ClickHouse for stats.

questions.title: Distributed Cache Design
questions.answer:
Key components:
1. Consistent Hashing: Map keys to nodes on a ring. Adding/removing a node only remaps ~K/N keys (vs. K/2 with simple modulo). Use virtual nodes for uniform distribution.
2. Replication: Each key stored on N nodes (e.g., 3). Reads from any replica. Writes to primary → async replication.
3. Eviction: LRU per shard with max memory limit. TTL expiry (lazy + active background sweep).
4. Cache Coherence: On write, invalidate all replicas (delete-on-write) or use versioned values (read-your-writes consistency).
5. Client-side routing: Clients use the same consistent hash ring to determine which node to contact — no central router bottleneck.

Redis Cluster in production implements this with 16384 hash slots distributed across master nodes, each with replicas.

questions.title: Scalable System for Very High QPS
questions.answer:
Layer by layer approach:
1. Client/CDN: Static assets cached at edge. CDN absorbs 60–70% of traffic before it hits origin.
2. API Gateway: Rate limiting, auth, request routing, SSL termination.
3. Load Balancer: L7 (Application LB) → round-robin / least-connections across stateless service instances. Auto-scaling group expands horizontally.
4. Services: Stateless microservices — no server-side session (JWT). Horizontally scalable.
5. Cache: Redis cluster in front of DB. Cache-aside for hot data. Target 95%+ cache hit rate.
6. DB: Read replicas for 80% read workload. Write to primary. Shard by user_id or booking_id for extreme scale.
7. Async: Non-critical work (emails, analytics, rewards) offloaded to Kafka → workers. Reduces synchronous API latency.
8. Circuit Breakers: Resilience4j on downstream calls. Fallback to stale cache or graceful degradation.

questions.title: Facebook Messenger / Chat System
questions.body: Naukri Code360 SDE-2 campus (Jul 2022). 1-on-1 + group chat, delivered/read receipts, offline message storage, push notifications, end-to-end encryption, media.
questions.answer: WebSocket for real-time. Fan-out on write for group chat. Message queue (Kafka) for delivery. Cassandra for message storage (wide column, time-series friendly).
